name: Swedish Meatballs
notes: Since Mom and Dad have discovered they BOTH have significant Swedish ancestry, a must-include in the family cookbook. Best made on a hot date.

steps.title: Form the meatballs
steps.body: Combine, and form into balls (about 1½ inches): **1 pound ground pork**, **1 pound ground beef**, **1 medium onion**, grated, **¼ flat leaf parsley**, minced, **½ tsp ground nutmeg**, **½ tsp ground allspice**, **2 tsp salt**, **½ pepper**, **4 cloves garlic**, **¾ cup panko** (bread crumbs) and **2 eggs**.

steps.title: Brown the meatballs
steps.body: Brown in frying pan, with **2 Tbsp olive oil**, about 5 min on each side, then set aside.

steps.title: Melt the butter
steps.body: After meatballs are browned, melt **½ cup butter** in the frying pan.

steps.title: Add the flour
steps.body: When butter begins to bubble, sprinkle in **½ cup flour**. Cook for 1 minute.

steps.title: Add the broth
steps.body: Add **4 cups beef broth**, a little at a time, and whisk until the broth is all incorporated.

steps.title: Season the gravy
steps.body: Add **1 tsp salt**, **¼ tsp pepper**, **1 Tbsp lemon juice**, **¼ tsp ground allspice**, **¼ tsp ground nutmeg** and **1 tsp brown mustard**.

steps.title: Add the cream
steps.body: Slowly whisk in **1 cup cream**, and warm, but do not boil.

steps.title: Simmer the meatballs
steps.body: Add meatballs to the gravy, and simmer 8-10 minutes.

steps.title: Serve
steps.body: Serve over mashed potatoes, rice, or egg noodles, with lingonberry jam, or cranberry relish (if you’re in a jam).
